items.prompt: One black pawn is missing from the first position (g7). White to move is thinking of Qxc8+ Bxc8 Rf8+. Does the queen sacrifice win? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Qxc8+ is far worse than the engine's best move.
The engine prefers the quiet check Qb2+.

hints: Count Black's pieces that can answer Rf8+ once the queen and bishop have been exchanged.
Ask where the black king can go after Rf8+.
The king has a flight square, so the check is not mate.
items.explain: Qxc8+ now loses at least four pawns' worth compared with the best move. The only change from the winning version is the missing pawn on g7. Whether a sacrifice works depends on the flight squares of the king.

feedback_by_move.c2c8: The same sacrifice that mates with a pawn on g7 fails here: the engine rates it far below the best move.

items.prompt: Black has no bishop on g4. White to move. Find the strongest move.

claims.statement: Qxc8+ is the engine's best move.
Qxc8+ leads to mate in two.
No black piece attacks c8, so nothing can recapture the queen.

hints: Is anything of White's actually given up here?
Look at who can recapture on c8.
Take the rook with check.
items.explain: Qxc8+ takes the rook with check and no black piece can recapture, so nothing is sacrificed. The engine finds mate in two. The same capture needed a sacrifice only when a bishop could recapture.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Qg8 is checkmate.
Qb8 is also checkmate.
Both mates are best.

hints: Which squares can the black king reach?
Which white piece guards g8?
Look for a check that cannot be captured.
items.explain: Qg8 is checkmate (so is Qb8): the knight on h6 guards g8, so the king cannot capture the queen. Nothing has to be given up first.

items.prompt: White to move. A black pawn has appeared on d7. Find a good move.

claims.statement: h5 and Rf1 are the engine's two best moves.
Be6 is far worse than the best moves here.

hints: What does the black pawn on d7 cover?
The plan that worked before the pawn arrived needs a second look.
A quiet move, not a bishop move.
items.explain: h5 and Rf1 are the best moves here (the engine rates them about equally). Be6, the strongest move without the pawn on d7, is now far worse: the pawn on d7 can take on e6. A defender already in place changes what the plan is worth.

feedback_by_move.g4e6: The plan from the version without the pawn does not work here: dxe6 is possible and the engine rates Be6 far below the best moves.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Nxh4 is the engine's best move.
Nxh4 wins the queen.

hints: Is any black piece loose?
Which white piece attacks the black queen?
Take the queen.
items.explain: The black queen is attacked by the knight and not defended, so Nxh4 simply wins it. No attack on a king is needed, so the question of how fast to attack does not arise.

hints: Is any white piece loose?

items.explain: The white queen is attacked by the knight and not defended, so Nxh5 wins it outright.

items.prompt: Black threatens Qxg2 mate. White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: If White passes, Black mates with Qxg2.
Rf2 is the engine's best move.
Qxf7+, the counter-attack that worked with a pawn on e6, is far worse here.

hints: What does Black threaten if White does nothing?
Count how many moves White needs for a counter-attack and how many Black needs.
Cover g2.
items.explain: Black threatens Qxg2 mate. Without the pawn on e6 the check on f7 can be captured, and the engine rates Qxf7+ far below Rf2, which meets the threat. A counter-attack needs its own forcing line; here it has none.

feedback_by_move.h5f7: With the pawn on e6 this check led to mate. Here the bishop on d5 can take it and the engine rates the move far below Rf2.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Qxf2 is the engine's best move.
Qf8+ is far worse here.

hints: Is anything of White's attacked, and what does it cost to remove the attacker?
Compare a forcing check with simply trading.
Take the queen.
items.explain: Qxf2 is best: it removes the queen that attacked White's rook. Qf8+, a mating attack in the version with a black knight on f4, is far worse here.

answer.outcome: Nothing to counter-attack with: hold the draw

claims.statement: The tablebase says the position is a draw for the side to move.
The engine rates it as level.

hints: Which pieces does Black have?
A counter-attack needs an attacker.
Black has only the king.
items.explain: Black has only a king, so there is nothing to counter-attack with. The task is purely to defend, and the tablebase says the defence holds: the position is a draw.
options: Nothing to counter-attack with: hold the draw

items.prompt: Black to move. A white knight stands on d4. Find the best move.

claims.statement: cxd4+ is the engine's best move.
The pawn lever c4 is far worse here.

hints: What does the pawn on c5 attack now?
Check what the new white knight attacks before you push.
Capture.
items.explain: cxd4+ is best. Without the knight, c4 won because the pawn attacked the queen on b3 and the rook on d3 at once (a pawn fork). The new knight on d4 attacks the black queen on c6, so after c4 White plays Nxc6, and the engine rates c4 far below cxd4+. Judge a pawn push by what it leaves attacked.

feedback_by_move.c5c4: Without the knight this push forked queen and rook. Now the knight attacks your queen, so Nxc6 comes first.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: White threatens Qxh5 mate.
g6 is the engine's best move.
The check Qd2+ is far worse.

hints: First name the threat. Then ask which resource meets it.
Check what happens to the queen after a check.

items.explain: g6 defends the pawn on h5, so Qxh5+ would lose the queen to gxh5. The check Qd2+ is not a counter-threat: White just captures the queen with Qxd2 or Bxd2.

feedback_by_move.a5d2: This check only loses the queen: Qxd2 or Bxd2 takes it, and the mate threat is still there.

items.prompt: Black to move. A white knight has come to g4. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Nd7 is the engine's best move.
g6 is far worse here.
If Black passes, Nf6+ gxf6 Qh5 is mate in two.

hints: Name the threat again: the position is not the same as before.
What does the knight on g4 attack?
A knight move.
items.explain: The knight on g4 blocks the queen's diagonal, so Qxh5 is no longer the threat. The new threat is Nf6+ gxf6 Qh5#. Nd7 covers f6 and is best; g6 answered the old threat and is now far worse. Name the chief threat again after every change.

feedback_by_move.g7g6: This worked before the knight arrived on g4. Now the engine rates it far below Nd7.
